item.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03603v1).

item.title: Giant Planet Mass Function Across Stellar Mass and: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Giant Planet Mass Function Across Stellar Mass and: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy: Although giant planet occurrence correlates with stellar mass and metallicity, it remains unclear whether these properties also shape the companion mass distribution. We investigate this question using 719 FGKM stars from the California Legacy Survey and companion true-mass constraints from radial velocities and Hipparcos-Gaia astrometry. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03613v1).

item.title: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics: We show that the vacuum partition function of the $q$-deformed oscillator \[ L_q(z):= \langle0|e^{zT_q}|0\rangle, \qquad T_q := \mathsf{a}_q + \mathsf{a}_q^* \] satisfies the Lee-Yang property, i.e., all zeros of $L_q$ lie on the imaginary line for all $q\in[-1, 1)$, proving the conjectures of Okuyama'23. Using the connection between $q$-deformed oscillators and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian in the doubly-scaled regime, we show that the annealed SYK partition function satisfies the Lee-Yang property in the thermodynamic limit, that is, all of its Fisher zeros are on the imaginary axis. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03624v1).

item.title: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03630v1).

item.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $τ=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03639v1).

item.title: Neptunian ridge through the lens of TESS: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Neptunian ridge through the lens of TESS: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy: The Neptunian desert and savanna are separated by a ridge, an overdensity at orbital periods of approximately 3-6 d identified with Kepler. Like the hot Jupiter pileup at larger radii, this feature has been linked to the accumulation of successful outcomes of high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03643v1).

item.title: Compressed Oracle Duality: A simple framework for: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Compressed Oracle Duality: A simple framework for: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: Given a quantum adversary that queries a random oracle, how do we characterize the information that they "know"? The Compressed Oracle method of Zhandry (CRYPTO 2019) is one method that records the queries that the adversary makes; this recording is a representation of the information that is learned. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00609v1).

item.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00620v1).

item.title: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps: New Evidence in Advanced Physics & Deep Science
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps: New Evidence in Advanced Physics & Deep Science: We determine exactly which gap labels are realized by open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants ($0<λ_1,λ_2\leq1$). When both couplings are strictly less than one, every permitted gap label is realized by an open gap, including in the critical case ($λ_1=λ_2$). Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42120v1).

item.title: Weighted hypergraph states as a resource for quantum: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Weighted hypergraph states as a resource for quantum: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: Quantum correlations can be used to improve sensing precision beyond classical limits, yet the correlated resource states needed can be challenging to prepare and preserve. Here, we study the family of weighted hypergraph states and identify subclasses characterized by their underlying graph topology that exhibit enhanced metrological performance. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42129v1).

item.title: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: We investigate the dynamics of quantum systems whose evolution is governed by linear generators of fixed unitarily invariant norm. For this broad class of evolutions, we derive a universal time-optimal generator of the dynamics converting one given state into another. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42131v1).

item.title: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: An unknown quantum operation, like an unknown quantum state, cannot be perfectly copied or stored for later use. A specific gate can be embedded in an entangled resource and teleported, but its destination is fixed when the resource is created. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42150v1).

item.title: Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion: New Evidence in Biophysics & Genomics: Interactions between floating wind turbines and the marine atmospheric boundary layer affect turbine wakes and power output. This study examines the impact of turbine representations and platform pitching motion on power predictions for aligned floating wind turbine arrays. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41224v1).

item.title: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41240v1).

item.title: Fast and Accurate Neural Triage Decoding [2026 Breakthrough]
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of: New Evidence in Quantum & Physics: Quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing. High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have emerged as a promising approach to reducing the substantial physical qubit overhead of quantum error correction, enabling encoding rates exceeding $1/2$ in blocks of approximately one thousand physical data qubits. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40490v1).

item.title: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time [Astrophysics]
item.dc:creator: BioGravity Science Bureau
item.description: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy: The angle between a star's rotational angular momentum vector and the orbital angular momentum vector of its planets---stellar obliquity---encodes the initial conditions and dynamical history of planetary systems. Variations in obliquity with orbital separation may arise from either primordial disk structure (e.g., broken or warped protoplanetary disks with misaligned inner and outer regions) or subsequent dynamical interactions with planets or external perturbers. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40527v1).

item.title: How Do Tall Trees Pull Water Against Gravity? Physics of Redwoods
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: At heights exceeding 380 feet (115 meters), California coast redwoods transport hundreds of gallons of water daily from soil to their crown against gravitational pull. Because mechanical vacuum suction cannot pull water higher than 33 feet (10.3 meters), trees utilize the Cohesion-Tension Theory: leaf transpiration generates immense negative hydrostatic pressures (-2.5 MPa) that pull water upward like unbroken microscopic steel cables.

item.title: The Fermi Paradox: If Aliens Exist, Where Is Everybody?
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: During a lunchtime conversation at Los Alamos in 1950, Nobel laureate Enrico Fermi asked a simple question: 'Where is everybody?' With over 100 billion stars in our galaxy and billions of Earth-like planets in habitable zones, an intelligent civilization with modest spaceflight capability should colonize the Milky Way within 50 million years. This dispatch explores the Great Filter, percolation theory, and the zoo hypothesis.

item.title: 3D Bioprinting Organs in Space: Why Zero-G Changes Everything
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: 3D bioprinting human organs in microgravity is vastly superior to terrestrial bioprinting because zero gravity prevents delicate living cells from collapsing under their own weight. On Earth, printing soft biological tissues (such as heart muscle, lung capillaries, and liver lobules) requires rigid synthetic scaffolds or toxic chemical crosslinkers to keep structures from flattening into puddles. In orbital weightlessness, low-viscosity bioinks remain perfectly suspended in 3D space, allowing fragile vascular capillaries and complex organoids to fuse naturally before returning to Earth.

item.title: Space Motion Sickness: Why 70% of Astronauts Suffer in Orbit
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: Space Adaptation Syndrome (SAS)—commonly known as space motion sickness—afflicts roughly 60% to 70% of all astronauts during their first 48 to 72 hours in microgravity. It is triggered by neuro-vestibular sensory conflict: while the inner ear's semicircular canals correctly detect head rotations, the otolith organs (which rely on gravity-weighted calcium carbonate crystals) fail to register downward pull. The brain receives violent contradictory signals between visual input and inner ear telemetry, resulting in nausea, headache, cold sweats, and sudden emesis.

item.title: Can Plants Grow in Space Without Gravity? NASA Astrobotany
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: Yes, plants can grow in space without gravity: multiple generations of crops—including red romaine lettuce, dwarf tomatoes, radishes, and wheat—have successfully germinated, flowered, and produced viable seeds aboard the International Space Station. While plants on Earth use gravity (gravitropism) to guide roots down and stems up, plants in microgravity adapt by relying heavily on light cues (phototropism) and moisture gradients (hydrotropism). The greatest technical challenge is not plant genetics, but managing water and oxygen in soil without gravity-driven drainage.

item.title: How Do Astronauts Sleep in Zero Gravity on the Space Station?
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: In space, astronauts sleep inside personal phone-booth-sized cabins (Crew Quarters) inside specialized padded sleeping bags firmly strapped to the walls or ceiling. Because there is no gravity, there is no physical 'up' or 'down', and astronauts require no mattress or pillow. Crucially, sleep stations must be continuously ventilated by forced air fans: without gravity-driven convection, exhaled carbon dioxide pools around an astronaut's face, creating a localized CO2 bubble that can cause severe headaches, carbon dioxide poisoning, and suffocation.

item.title: Why Astronauts Lose 1-2% Bone Density Every Month in Space
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: Astronauts lose bone density in space because their skeleton is completely unloaded in microgravity: without the continuous downward mechanical stress of body weight, bone-building cells (osteoblasts) shut down, while bone-resorbing cells (osteoclasts) continue actively breaking down bone matrix. Astronauts lose between 1.0% to 1.5% of bone mineral density in weight-bearing bones (lumbar spine, hips, and femurs) for every month in orbit—a rate 10 to 12 times faster than severe postmenopausal osteoporosis on Earth.

item.title: Zero Gravity vs Microgravity: The Difference Explained
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: The fundamental difference is that 'zero gravity' does not exist in Low Earth Orbit: at the altitude of the International Space Station (~400 km), Earth's gravitational pull is still roughly 90% as strong as it is on the surface. Astronauts float not because gravity is absent, but because the station travels sideways at 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h)—falling toward Earth at the exact same rate that the planet's surface curves away beneath it. This continuous free-fall state is scientifically termed 'microgravity' (typically 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁶ g).

item.title: How Does Zero Gravity Kill Cancer Cells? Space Oncology Research
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: Zero gravity kills cancer cells by disabling their mechanical survival machinery: without gravity's constant shear force, cancer cells fail to sense external mechanical tension, causing their actin stress fibers and microtubule cytoskeletons to depolymerize. In multiple space station and microgravity experiments, this physical collapse triggers programmed cell death (apoptosis) in up to 80% to 90% of aggressive tumor cells (including breast, ovarian, and melanoma lines) within 24 to 48 hours without chemotherapy.

item.title: What Happens to the Human Body in Zero Gravity? Medical Guide
item.dc:creator: Dr. Elena Vance
item.description: In zero gravity, the human body undergoes immediate and deep changes: approximately 2 liters of fluid shift upwards into the head and chest (causing 'puffy face bird-legs syndrome'), the spine stretches up to 2 inches due to lack of spinal compression, bones lose 1% to 1.5% of their mineral density each month, and the heart shrinks slightly because it no longer needs to pump blood against gravity.
